title: George and the Wellerman — lyric slideshow

frames.text: There once was a ship that put to sea
frames.action: Wide dawn shot of Billy o' Tea leaving harbour into open sea. Faces may be small silhouettes.
frames.continuity_note: Opening. Same five people aboard; distant.

frames.text: The name of that ship was the Billy o' Tea
frames.action: Medium shot of the same ship. George near the mast, Captain at the stern, three crew at the rigging. Tea-leaf emblem clear.
frames.continuity_note: Same ship and five people; camera closer.

frames.text: The winds blew hard, her bow dipped down
frames.action: Bow plunges into a wave. George and crew-stocky grip the bow rail. Captain midships. crew-red and crew-young hold lines farther aft.
frames.continuity_note: All five still on the mother ship; George + crew-stocky at the bow.

frames.text: Blow, my bully boys, blow (huh)
frames.action: George, crew-red, crew-young and crew-stocky lean back on one thick rope, cheering. Captain watches from the stern.
frames.continuity_note: First close lineup of the three Billy crew faces.

frames.text: Soon may the Wellerman come
frames.action: Billy five crane their necks, excited and hopeful, not idle. crew-stocky and crew-red lower a thick rope down Billy's side for the incoming ship. George waves both arms. Captain points at Wellerman. The smaller Wellerman is actively rowing and sailing TOWARD Billy with a bow wake. supply-beard and supply-cap pull oars, looking at Billy, working, not standing with hands in pockets. Cargo 3 pale crates PORT, 2 dark chests MID, 4 barrels STARBOARD. No whale.
frames.continuity_note: Supply pair first locked. Same faces on all remaining Wellerman frames (6, 21, 22).

frames.text: To bring us sugar and tea and rum
frames.action: Alongside transfer. supply-beard passes a tea chest; supply-cap steadies a rum barrel. George claps; crew-stocky reaches for a crate. Captain supervises. crew-red and crew-young hold alignment lines on Billy.
frames.continuity_note: Same supply pair and cargo style; only motion is passing goods.

frames.text: One day, when the tonguing's done
frames.action: ONLY Billy o' Tea. Historical tonguing like parent photo: a large DARK rounded whale body lies on the wet deck. A huge pale creamy BLUBBER BLANKET is being peeled off that body and hoisted nearly vertical by mast ropes hooked into the top of the flap. crew-red, crew-young and crew-stocky lean into long-handled spades at the cut-line where pale fat meets the dark body. Captain hauls the tackle, straining. George pulls a smaller rope, determined not smiling. Overcast sky, exhausting labour. No blood, no red tissue, no guts, no Wellerman, no swimming whale in the sea.
evidence: pale blanket peeling off the body
men at the cut-line leaning hard
George on a rope not smiling
frames.continuity_note: Tonguing matches historical flensing (parent photo). Chorus pair with lyric-23. Child-safe: pale blubber, no gore.

frames.text: We'll take our leave and go
frames.action: All five on Billy's stern waving goodbye as the ship sails toward the horizon. Wake visible.
frames.continuity_note: Wellerman leaves the frame. Same five on Billy. Pair with lyric-24.

frames.text: She had not been two weeks from shore
frames.action: Reuses lyric-17 art: weary forty-day hunt mood on Billy only. Captain at the wheel worried; crew-young scans empty horizon with a telescope; crew-stocky scrubs the deck; crew-red sweeps; George helps with a small broom, worried frown. No coastline needed. No Wellerman, no whale, no calendar.
frames.continuity_note: Parent: same picture as lyric-17 (For forty days). Same five aboard.

frames.text: When down on her a right whale bore
frames.action: Right whale surfaces on the starboard side with V-spray. George grips the rail, surprised. Captain and crew-stocky at the rail; crew-red and crew-young run closer but stay on deck.
evidence: callosities on snout, above left eye, right jaw
frames.continuity_note: First close whale. All five still on mother ship; nobody in the whaleboat.

frames.text: The Captain called all hands and swore
frames.action: Stern captain in the centre, waving or whistling. Three crew run toward him from different directions. George watches from the side. Stern, not smiling.
frames.continuity_note: Sets up the split: red+young will take the boat; stocky stays on deck.

frames.text: He'd take that whale in tow (huh)
frames.action: Tow line stretches toward the free whale but is not attached. crew-red and crew-young stand beside Whaleboat-1 still on davits. crew-stocky at the davits. George holds a rope coil. Captain points at the whale.
evidence: whaleboat on davits empty of seated crew
frames.continuity_note: Boat still empty. Same pair who will sit in it next frame.

frames.text: Before the boat had hit the water
frames.action: Whaleboat-1 hanging from davits, hull not yet touching the sea. crew-red at the bow seat, crew-young at the stern seat. George, Captain and crew-stocky lower ropes from the mother-ship deck.
frames.continuity_note: ONLY allowed whaleboat crew. Occupancy locked through lyric-16.

frames.text: The whale's tail came up and caught her
frames.action: Huge fluke slaps spray. Whaleboat tilts but does not capsize. Same two men grip the gunwales. Mother-ship trio watch from starboard.
frames.continuity_note: Boat occupants must match lyric-13 exactly.

frames.text: All hands to the side, harpooned and fought her
frames.action: All hands: mother-ship trio lean over the starboard rail; boat pair raise rope-harpoon poles toward the whale. Poles do not touch the whale's skin.
frames.continuity_note: All hands means deck trio PLUS the same boat pair — no teleport swap.

frames.text: When she dived down low (huh)
frames.action: Whale dives whole-body. Line races past the boat but does not bind the whale. George points at bubble trail from the mother ship. Same boat pair still in Whaleboat-1.
frames.continuity_note: Last occupied-boat frame. Next lyric is forty days later; pair return to deck.

frames.text: For forty days or even more
frames.action: Forty days of hunting with no catch. Only Billy o' Tea on an empty sea. All five look weary and worried, not smiling. Captain grips the helm and steers with a furrowed brow. crew-young stands at the rail scanning the empty horizon with a brass telescope. crew-stocky scrubs the wooden deck on his knees. crew-red sweeps with a broom. George in sailor suit helps with a small broom, worried frown, not a toothy grin. No Wellerman, no supply men, no cargo stacks, no whale in the water, no calendar or number 40.
frames.continuity_note: Time skip: boat pair legally back on Billy. This is the long fruitless hunt — Wellerman has not arrived yet in this shot.

frames.text: The line went slack then tight once more
frames.action: crew-stocky at the winch manages a coil that visibly goes slack then taut. George watches the coil. Captain at stern. crew-red and crew-young help pull. No Wellerman.
frames.continuity_note: Line handler is always crew-stocky, not a new face.

frames.text: All boats were lost, there were only four
frames.action: Four intact empty whaleboats remain. TWO hang from davits on the PORT side and TWO hang from davits on the STARBOARD side (or stern) — never four davits in a single row on one rail. Extra empty davits split on both sides show losses. Five people on deck count the remaining boats. No numeral 4.
evidence: davits on BOTH sides of the ship
not four hooks in one row
frames.continuity_note: Whaleboat-1 style matches lyric-13. Nobody seated in boats. Davits must look like a real whaler, port and starboard.

frames.text: And still that whale did go (huh)
frames.action: Billy five watch the same whale swim away, tail fluke up, no rope on the animal. ONLY Billy o' Tea — no Wellerman, no supply men, no cargo. Gentle humour, not anger.
frames.continuity_note: Whale still the same animal (callosities). The whale has gone; the supply ship is not in this shot.

frames.text: Soon may the Wellerman come
frames.action: Same eager scene as lyric-05 from a slightly lower deck angle: Billy five crane necks, lower a rope; Wellerman rows toward Billy; same two supply men working oars; same cargo layout. No whale.
frames.continuity_note: Chorus pair with lyric-05. Camera angle may change; people and cargo may not.

frames.text: To bring us sugar and tea and rum
frames.action: Same transfer as lyric-06: supply-beard passes tea, supply-cap steadies rum, George claps, crew-stocky receives.
frames.continuity_note: Chorus pair with lyric-06.

frames.text: One day, when the tonguing's done
frames.action: Same historical tonguing as lyric-07, slightly different angle: dark whale body on deck, pale blubber blanket peeling off, mast ropes hoisting the flap, three crew at the cut-line, captain and George hauling. No blood, no Wellerman, no swimming whale.
evidence: pale blanket peeling off the body
men at the cut-line leaning hard
frames.continuity_note: Chorus pair with lyric-07.

frames.text: We'll take our leave and go
frames.action: Same five waving from Billy's stern as lyric-08. Optional warm sunset. No Wellerman.
frames.continuity_note: Chorus pair with lyric-08. Sunset is the only allowed change.
